quest.title: Crimes One and Two
quest.description: The Windblume Festival should be a joyous affair, but not all is as it seems in Mondstadt...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Sara
dialogues.text: Happy Windblume! What can I get for you?

dialogues.speaker: Norma
dialogues.text: Hm, let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'd be grateful if you could keep an eye on things during the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Wyratt
dialogues.text: This office is now off limits. You need Master Jean's permission to enter.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Beatrice... *sigh* What's going on with her...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, the city is all decked out! Aww, it's beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Festival season means no commissions, which means no Mora... But, Katheryne's always looking out for us, so we should still drop by and say hello!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Greetings {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Katheryne! Still doing the whole "no commissions during Windblume" thing?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: In general, yes. The people of Mondstadt don't delegate their work to others this time of year. But...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Feel free to take a look around. I think you'll pick up on something unusual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take a look around, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: ...*sigh*. It's finally Windblume, and here I am, ruining everything...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: You're a bit tired, no big deal. Give it some time. How about doing something fun tonight? We could take a stroll or go star-gazing?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Star-gazing? Like we'll find a spot... You know people start reserving places on Starsnatch Cliff the moment the sun goes down... *sigh* Sorry, I'm just... not in the mood. I should go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, something's off with Beatrice. She would never give up a chance to talk to Quinn. This is weird.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Oh, you're leaving? I can walk you home...

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: No, it's okay... thank you. I just need some time to myself. Besides, there's still something... I need to do.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: The truth is, Quinn... Not long ago, I...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: What is it? Is there something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: ...Never mind. It's nothing. Actually, Quinn, I... I think we should stop seeing each other for now.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait... are you saying we can't be friends anymore? I thought we were best friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you see that? Beatrice ran off without looking back... We go adventuring in other nations for a bit, and one of Mondstadt's best love — er, friendship — stories is already over?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, is this what you meant by "unusual," Katheryne?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: This is just one example. Beatrice has been feeling down for days. But, that's not all.

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Oh, it's the Honorary Knight and Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is something wrong? You don't look so good...

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: *sigh* I know, a Knight should be stronger than this. But, I haven't been feeling right lately. I—I just can't focus...

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: I started sleepwalking out of nowhere. Sometimes, I'd even wake up in the middle of the night standing in a random location outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You should see a doctor!

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: I did! But, all the tests came back normal. The doctor said I'm fine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Strange...

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Yeah... I even consulted Miss Barbara at the church, but her conclusion was the same. In any case, she was kind enough to pray to Lord Barbatos for me to get better.

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: ...Is it because I saw something I wasn't meant to see?

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Ah, sorry. This is for me to figure out. It is Windblume, after all. Anyway, I have a patrol to finish. Until next time, you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, is it something in the air, maybe?

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: ...*sigh*.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It appears Miss Donna is also out of sorts...

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: *sigh* Where can I find a truly fascinating man...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but Donna is the one who has a huge crush on Diluc, right?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: That's what I thought, too, but she seems to have changed her mind.

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: Hmm? Is that... Captain Kaeya?

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: Huh... Now I look at him, he's exactly my type. How come I never felt this way before?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I'm flattered, Miss Donna. Although, I do wonder whether that was intended for outside ears...

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: Oh, no. Of course not, I... I'm sorry, Captain. Just pretend I didn't say anything! And, um... Have a happy Windblume!

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I intend to, my dear. But, first a question, if you don't mind. Why the sudden change of heart? I was under the impression Master Diluc was the object of your affections...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Good question, Kaeya!)

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: So, you knew about that... Well, Master Diluc came into the city not too long ago, but when I saw him, it was like... the butterflies just weren't there anymore.

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: If I had to compare it to something, it would be like... waking up and realizing you're married to a man you don't love.

response.speaker: Donna
response.text: But, then I saw you, and it wasn't that something was different about you. I can't really explain it. It was just... a feeling!

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I understand, and I'm flattered I was able to bring back the butterflies. But, I do need to see to some business, so I'll take my leave.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Here he comes. Hehe, well? Surprised to see us?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: #Not at all. You are the exact two people I've been trying to find. So, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, how have you been?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: All good. How about yourself and the rest of the Knights of Favonius?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: The answer to that... requires a private conversation. Katheryne, do you mind?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Not at all. Have fun, you three.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you said you were looking for us?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Yes, Jean sent me to find you when she heard you were back in Mondstadt. But, let's discuss the finer details back at headquarters.

choices.text: Maybe they're just working out the kinks...

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: It's festival season again! I wonder what this year's Windblume is going to be.

dialogues.speaker: Eury
dialogues.text: I know! I can't wait to find out!

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Ah, Kaeya. You found them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Yep. I managed to track them down.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Good. With what's about to happen, it's great to have you in town.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, headquarters are packed... What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Note
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, Paimon, it's an honor to meet you. I believe introductions are in order.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Allow me. You have Note, Captain of the 2nd Company. Skeiron, Captain of the 3rd Company. Eula, Captain of the 4th Company. And me, of course, Captain of the 9th Company.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you're all captains?

dialogues.speaker: Skeiron
dialogues.text: That's right. Master Jean is waiting for you inside. She'll explain everything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jean!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, thank you for coming.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is everything alright? There are tons of people outside.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, that would be the captains. You know a few of them already, but I'm sure there are some new faces.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: There have been a number of... incidents in Mondstadt. In order to wrap up the case, I gathered all the captains of the Knights of Favonius together to hold a trial.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A trial? But, this is Mondstadt, not Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I can understand the confusion. You've never participated in one of our trials before. In truth, we haven't had to conduct one in quite some time...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius oversee most matters of law and order in Mondstadt. Of course, in the interest of fairness, major cases are tried jointly with the Church.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Under the guidance of Barbatos, the Knights uphold chivalric justice in the spirit of our order, and the Church carries blessings and goodwill wherever the wind can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: And today's case... requires a joint trial by both parties.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Which means it's a serious one. So, do you need our help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hold on. The group of people we saw in the corridor just now... There was someone missing...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where's Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! He's the Captain of the Investigation Team! But, we didn't see him out there.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #...A keen observation, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: That happens to be exactly why I called you here.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: In the upcoming trial against Captain Albedo, we will do our utmost to understand the facts of this case and deliver a fair and impartial verdict.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo is the one on trial!? What did he do?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Jean, it's time.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #Understood. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Wyratt
dialogues.text: Wait, Captain Kaeya! Surely, I can't just—

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: These two are here on Jean's orders. She asked them to investigate Albedo's office.

dialogues.speaker: Wyratt
dialogues.text: Oh, in that case... Head on in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this is Albedo's office... Pretty much exactly how Paimon pictured it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Alright, I have some work of my own, so I'll leave you to it. Good luck, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right back at you!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Please, sit wherever you like. I only ask that you remain calm, no matter what you hear. I need to head over there.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Don't worry. The trial will be fair.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: ...Now that everyone is gathered, let us begin.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: With Grand Master Varka away from Mondstadt for the time being, I, Jean Gunnhildr, will oversee today's proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Mr. Dahlia, Deacon of the Church of Favonius, will serve as assessor. As representatives of our respective organizations, we will ensure a just verdict in this case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's a new face. Deacon of the Church... Does that mean he works with Barbara and Rosaria?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The defendant in today's case is the Captain of the Investigation Team, Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Albedo... What did you do?)

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Certain aspects of this case are classified, and it remains uncertain whether the alleged victims are citizens of Mondstadt. As such, this trial is not open to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The identities of the victims are still unknown? Strange.)

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: If guilt is established in this case, all facts will be made public after the final verdict is delivered.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Now, the Captain of the Logistics Company, Miss Hertha, will present the charges. The court appoints Mr. Kaeya to speak on Mr. Albedo's behalf. Are both parties ready to proceed?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Ready to proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Miss Hertha, the floor is yours.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Prior to this trial, the Knights of Favonius, in conjunction with the Church, launched an investigation into Mr. Albedo for suspected murder and unlawful disposal of human remains.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Murder!?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: A witness stated that, eleven days ago in the middle of the night, she saw the defendant southeast of the city gates, dragging a large object she later identified as a human body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No... There's no way...

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: We now call that witness to the stand. Beatrice, please tell us what you saw.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Beatrice... So, is that what she was trying to tell Quinn earlier?)

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Well, I was out late that night on business. And, when I came back, I saw someone in the moonlight that looked like Mr. Albedo. He... He was dragging a huge bag of some kind.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I thought it was strange, so I followed him. Then, there was a sudden flash of golden light. The bag opened, and inside there was... there was a body.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Mr. Albedo's Vision allows him to manipulate the ground with ease. So, he buried it and then removed any traces on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Before he left, it seemed like he looked in my direction. Maybe it was just my imagination, but I was terrified, thinking he might kill me too... Luckily, he didn't see me.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I now turn to the defendant. Describe your whereabouts that night.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I was working in my office on the second floor of the Knights of Favonius headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: That's right. The next day, the defendant submitted his latest environmental report on the Dragonspine region. Considering the length of the text, it must have taken a considerable amount of time to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Can anyone attest to the fact that the defendant was working in his office that night?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Then, the length of the report is not a sufficient alibi.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: This isn't looking good.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: If the crime did occur as you described, then what about the body? You mentioned the joint investigation. Well, was the body recovered?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: ...Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: In other words, you dug up the location Miss Beatrice described and found nothing. You don't find that suspicious?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I know what I saw!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I'm telling the truth, Miss Hertha, I swear! Also, didn't you say that speaking out would help protect the people of Mondstadt? Otherwise, I... I'd never put myself out here like this...

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: You're doing the right thing. Besides, the investigation wasn't fruitless. A single men's shoe and a torn piece of fabric were found in the bushes near the crime scene.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: The same location the witness described. If no crime occurred, then is all this just a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: And, yet, no victim has been identified, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: It's true, no one has been reported missing. However, Miss Beatrice harbors no ill will toward the defendant. Her testimony clearly points to a crime, and she has no reason to lie.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Does the defendant wish to say anything in response?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You may believe otherwise, Miss Hertha, but I did not kill a single person.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As a Knight and the Captain of the Investigation Team, I have a duty to protect Mondstadt and its people. You accuse me of murder, but there's no body... or motive.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: The defendant raises an important point — motive. Yet, I must be frank... not all murders are premeditated. Spontaneous conflict can also have unforeseen consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, I don't intend to prosecute this case on circumstantial evidence alone. Which brings me to the second charge against Mr. Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Second charge!?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Please proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Seven days ago, at dawn, a witness saw the defendant dispose of the body of an adult male in the area between Dragonspine and Dawn Winery.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: I now call the second witness to the stand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! That's...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: ...Diluc Ragnvindr.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Please tell the court what you saw.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: At around 3:40 in the morning, I saw Mr. Albedo dispose of a body beneath a cliff. It was dark, but he used the power of Geo to illuminate his surroundings.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: From what I could tell, it looked like the body of an adult male — tall and thin, but I couldn't make out the age. He buried the body underneath the cliff and smoothed out the ground to remove any traces.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: We now have accounts from two separate witnesses that describe the same modus operandi. Would you call that a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I would only inquire as to what Mr. Diluc was doing in that area so early in the morning. Not the most opportune time for a stroll...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Is there such a thing? Dawn Winery is my home. It's not unusual for me to take walks in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I just happened to be in the right place at the right time... that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Master Diluc is a well-respected figure in Mondstadt. I see no reason for him to frame Mr. Albedo. Yet, the question remains... Where are the bodies?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Before you suggest a lack of evidence, Mr. Kaeya, you should know — after the defendant left that morning, the witness found this where the body was buried.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: And this is...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: What looks like the teeth and femur of a human. Now, it does beg the question... If the burial was fresh, why is this all that remains of the body? But, I suppose Mr. Albedo is the only one who can answer that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: ...Careful now, Master Diluc. I do believe I hear a presumption of guilt in there somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: These remains suggest an accelerated rate of decomposition. Considering the defendant's profession, there's reason to suspect that alchemy is at play here.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Both witnesses saw golden light — a known by-product of alchemy. That's how the defendant destroyed the bodies. The light also explains how the witnesses were able to get a clear view of the events in the dark.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, that's your angle... Alchemy.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: A logical assessment, but we have a witness of our own. The afternoon before the alleged second murder, Mr. Albedo had a lengthy intellectual exchange with his student, Sucrose. The two were in the library until the next morning.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Why did the discussion last so long?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Miss Sucrose was presenting the results of her research. She noticed some flaws in the data, and insisted on reviewing her calculations until the next morning, with Mr. Albedo present.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That's right! We were in the library together!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: You're certain Mr. Albedo was present the whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes! And, I... I know Mr. Albedo would never kill someone! He could never be that cruel!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, the other witnesses have no reason to lie. Tell me, Miss Sucrose — that meeting in the library... Were you awake the whole time? Sounds like a considerable duration to go without sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, um... I...

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: I do hope you can be truthful with us — it concerns the safety of countless Mondstadt citizens. A crime like this cannot go unpunished.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll take it from here... During our meeting, Sucrose did fall asleep not long after midnight.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's alright, Sucrose. You don't have to lie for me. This is a sacred place of judgment — the truth is paramount.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Mr. Albedo...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I see. Then, I'm afraid your alibi cannot be substantiated. Do you understand?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. I know claiming innocence without proof isn't enough.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But, the prosecution's argument has its own holes. There's been no mention of a motive, or what exact method could reduce a human body to those remains.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Hm, no conclusive evidence of guilt, but the witness accounts do match to an extent that can't be dismissed... This is a tricky one.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Allow me to submit another piece of evidence. The investigators intercepted one of Mr. Albedo's correspondences. I will now read the pertinent parts to the court.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A correspondence...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: (Oh, no... That envelope does look like it belongs to Mr. Albedo...)

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: "I have never abandoned the subject of human research. In fact, delving deeper into Dragonspine has led me to realize that the concept of 'life' could be further expanded and transformed into that of 'birth.'"

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: "The mystery of human birth is often linked to death. As such, death is the most suitable material for the creation of new life. To that end, we must engage in a process of putrefaction and refinement."

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Putrefaction ... and refinement...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: ...Is that in reference to an alchemical process?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: The letter continues, "Experimental trials have been carried out in the northwestern part of Dragonspine and the area southeast of Mondstadt's main gate. The data is as expected."

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: "Just as you endeavored to do, I, too, shall take up the path of creation and break through current limitations to reach a new realm of 'living beings'."

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I trust the investigators have confirmed this to be the defendant's handwriting, and that the letter makes more than passing mention of "putrefaction" and "refinement."

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Correct. Not to mention, the locations indicated in the letter match both crime scenes. What more can we trust than the defendant's own words?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No... It can't be true...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I... I can't believe it...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: A guilty verdict cannot be delivered without sufficient evidence. In order to protect all parties involved, that is what our principles demand. My original assessment was that we lacked said evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: But, now, it seems the only remaining questions are the identities of the victims and the specific alchemical process used in this case.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hah.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: ...Then, we are in agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The evidence is conclusive. On the charges of murder and unlawful disposal of human remains, the court finds the defendant... guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The people in attendance appear shocked. No one can believe a kind and well-mannered person like Albedo could commit such a crime.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jean stipulates that those unsatisfied with the verdict will have time to submit an objection or appeal. But, most appear hopeless in this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you watch Albedo being taken back to headquarters, you get a strange feeling that something hidden is about to come to light...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It all comes back to the letter... a secret that you and Albedo know all too well, but the people of Mondstadt have yet to discover.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why would Albedo do something like that? This has to be a nightmare...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Albedo told me his secret once — that he was a synthetic human created through alchemy. Could that have something to do with this case?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But, what? Following in Rhinedottir's footsteps just because he's an alchemical creation? That would only make him more suspicious...)

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Well, this took a turn for the worse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rosaria! When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I've been here the whole time. I happen to have a message to pass along.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For us?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Yes. You're needed at Starsnatch Cliff. He's waiting for you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who is "he"?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: You'll know when you get there. Go on, now. Time is like the wind — it waits for no one.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I could hear your arrival upon the wind. Were you looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Venti! Did you send us that message?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: No, I did.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, where did you come from? Wait, Venti, do you know this guy? His name is... Um... what is his name again?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Didn't think I was that unmemorable... I'm Dahlia, Deacon of the Church of Favonius and Herald of the Anemo Archon, Barbatos. Not gonna forget next time, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you called us here so we could meet with Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: That's right. I noticed you during the trial... the legendary Honorary Knight. You seemed to have a lot of thoughts on your mind, so I thought we should have a chat.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: After all, I AM the Herald of Barbatos... If the people of Mondstadt are in danger, I should keep the Anemo Archon in the loop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, then... You know about...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Hahaha... About what? The fact that my tavern-hopping, nomad of a friend is Barbatos himself?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Don't worry — Dahlia and I are close. He knows everything.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Besides, a god needs someone to communicate their will in a formal setting, and no one does that better than Dahlia.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Not that I saw that coming when we first met... But, back to the matter at hand. I believe you two already know about Albedo's background.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you mean his true identity, then yeah, we do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you know, too, Venti? That's surprisingly Archon-like of you...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, well, I knew from the moment Rhinedottir and Alice brought Albedo to Mondstadt. When those two are in town, no one can afford to slack off.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The Kreideprinz, a perfect specimen of synthetic life... At this stage of the case, there are countless questions surrounding Albedo's motive. His true identity is a potential weakness.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: A synthetic being loses control of their sanity and goes on a killing spree... That's how a novel would frame the story, and people are inclined to agree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo has told us before that humans often value the "ordinary" over the "transcendent" and "miraculous."

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: And the slightest "difference" is perceived as "other" — a very common phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Which means, we need to find a way to help your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you know about the situation, Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Me? Well, I know that Albedo is a synthetic being, and that a lot of strange things have been happening in Mondstadt, even though Windblume should be about drinking and having fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We noticed that, too! The minute we got here, something was off.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share your observations with Venti and Dahlia...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I've picked up on most of those, too. Miles is out of sorts, Beatrice seems anxious... Although, I didn't know Donna stopped being interested in Master Diluc.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "When no love remains for the songs to tell, the world becomes naught but an empty shell. Cruel is said fate, cruel it may be, were it not for a hero who could set us all free..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you getting at, Tone-Deaf Bard?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, just making a comment. There are always unavoidable trials in life. At least, that's what Barbatos would say.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: A certain someone is going to need to overcome a trial like that. In such cases, even The Seven know better than to tamper with fate.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only there was a brave soul willing to aid their friend in his time of need? Should he meet a terrible fate, all of Mondstadt could be worse for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you wanted our help, you could've just asked, y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, well, even if Albedo wasn't at the center of this case, protecting Mondstadt is part of being an Honorary Knight, right?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You'll still have help, of course, which is why I prepared a little surprise, hehe... Behold!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A bomb!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Paimon remembers that Jumpy Dumpty!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Don't worry — I removed the fuse, so it's not going to explode. Say hello to the Dodocommunication Device.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this thing belongs to you now?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, we're old pals. Don't think she'd care if I borrowed it for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Anyway, this invention, with a little help from a trick of mine, will allow us to keep in touch. Just take it out, and we can chat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll do our best to uncover the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: That's all I ask. No matter what comes, you have the wind on your side.

talks.objective: Return to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I know you all must be shocked, but the evidence is solid. Albedo's situation... is not looking good.

dialogues.speaker: Skeiron
dialogues.text: I still don't believe Albedo would do something like that... Using living people as alchemical test subjects? It's like something out of a novel!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Perhaps it's best for me to remain impartial, but I've worked with Albedo before... He's an alchemist, not a sadist.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This version of events is as hard for me to accept as anyone. But... Varka once said Albedo is very different from the rest of us. Perhaps there are things we still need to learn about him...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Let's see what Albedo has to say for himself first. Would you mind giving me a moment, everyone? A private matter requires my attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Jean!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, perfect timing. Kaeya has a favor to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Like Jean said after the verdict, we have time to submit an appeal, and I will do my utmost to convince Albedo to accept.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: He's been acting strange, and I can't read him for the life of me... But, I need you two to start investigating the case.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Investigate the case?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Yes, it's also time for you to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you want us to join the joint investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: No — we'd like you to launch an investigation of your own. I'll continue working on his defense in the meantime. If you find anything that might help his case, just let me know.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I know it's against the spirit of the season to task you with this... But, Albedo is a trusted member of our ranks. We owe him the benefit of the doubt.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: #I know you'll get to the bottom of this, {NICKNAME}. You've never failed us in our time of need.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, what if the accusations turn out to be true?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Then, you will have done Mondstadt a great service all the same.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I'm expecting a retrial. Until then, you're welcome to have a look around Albedo's office on the second floor. I'm counting on you.

choices.text: I'll look into the case on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see what we can find.

response.speaker: Investigate the Test Tube
response.text: There's a test tube on the shelf with some black powder residue at the bottom.

response.speaker: Investigate the Test Tube
response.text: Next to it lies a neatly written note:

response.speaker: Investigate the Test Tube
response.text: "'Chalk' is the next stage after 'soil,' but the current available materials are still insufficient to construct a stable structure."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, no idea what that means... Not sure if it's too hard for Paimon, or too hard for anyone outside this line of work...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, that seems to be it for this place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should go tell Jean what we found.

response.speaker: Investigate the Book
response.text: There's a stack of books on the desk, mostly relating to alchemy, environmental science, and life science.

response.speaker: Investigate the Book
response.text: Some of the pages have been marked with alchemical symbols, and others have s-shaped or triangular symbols drawn on them. Any potential meaning is unclear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, these books are so... fancy. Albedo must have gone to great lengths to get them...

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Book
response.text: After moving the book, the desk looks almost empty.

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Book
response.text: Your hand slipped while moving the book, causing the hardcover book to strike the desk. The resulting noise is a bit unusual.

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Book
response.text: It's subtle, but to an experienced adventurer, it sounds too hollow. Almost like... there's a compartment within the desk.

choices.text: Investigate the lock box on the desk

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: A lock box sits on the desk. The latch bears signs of wear, suggesting the importance of whatever lies within — the box likely remained locked most of the time.

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: But, now, the lid remains wide open, as if the owner was forced to leave in a hurry and didn't have time to lock it.

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: Perhaps the letter intercepted by the investigators was once stored here. The remaining contents shouldn't hold much weight as conclusive evidence, but you still get a strange feeling after reviewing them.

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: In elegant penmanship, the letter reads, "...In addition, I do happen to have some information on the subject of our last discussion — the materials and arcane formation required for human transmutation."

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: "The formations in these records likely originate from the Khaenri'ahn art of Khemia. But, relevant documentation has not been well-maintained over time, so I cannot guarantee there are no errors or omissions. As thanks for your past assistance, I've enclosed the records with this letter."

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: "But, that does not mean I support your pursuit of this research. Ethics aside, I'm not convinced it's even possible to create a 'human' whose existence is identical to our own."

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: "The idea that the dynamic of creator and creation could exist within the same species is cause for concern. Even with a talent like yours, I must urge you to proceed with caution."

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: The signature belongs to an unfamiliar name, one that also appears on an alchemy book nearby. You skim the preface and learn that the author is an old and accomplished alchemist.

response.speaker: Investigate the Lock Box on the Desk
response.text: The person is likely a friend from Albedo's academic circle — someone who owed Albedo a favor, but also urged him to refrain from conducting dangerous research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Human transmutation? Is Albedo seriously looking into that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Paimon doesn't want to think about that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It doesn't look good, but this letter can't directly prove that Albedo did anything.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Besides, a technique like that must be too dangerous to share with the public, right? That's why it wasn't brought up during the trial.)

response.speaker: Investigate the Research Notes on the Desk
response.text: Albedo's notes lie on the table. They resemble the ones you've seen before, but the contents are different this time.

response.speaker: Investigate the Research Notes on the Desk
response.text: As always, the penmanship is impeccable, careful and neat with a certain elegance in its uniformity — much like the man himself.

response.speaker: Investigate the Research Notes on the Desk
response.text: One of the notes reads, "Putrefaction should be regarded as a counter-simulation to the process of life — like a highly efficient and destructive spell of rot."

response.speaker: Investigate the Research Notes on the Desk
response.text: "Upon use, the target will decay within an extremely short period of time, turning into dust that is nearly invisible to the naked eye before dissipating into the air."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, it looks like there's a hidden compartment under the desk!

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Desk
response.text: There does appear to be a compartment added to one side of the desk. It was very well-hidden.

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Desk
response.text: The lock mechanism is complex and seems to involve elemental power in some way. Perhaps you could try using the power of Geo...

response.speaker: Investigate Underneath the Desk
response.text: The hidden compartment opens. Inside lies a piece of paper with more information.

response.speaker: Investigate the Paper
response.text: "Festering is also a manifestation of rot."

response.speaker: Investigate the Paper
response.text: "When festering forces and a sufficient amount of life energy collide, the two will repel each other, triggering a powerful side effect. When I tested this in an alchemical experiment, the results of the refinement were startling."

response.speaker: Investigate the Paper
response.text: "Breaking through the shackles of life, the simulation of the ■■■■ Project... I must take advantage of this opportunity."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The name of the project is blotted out in ink... What could it be?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The note mentioned "festering forces," which suggests that Dragonspine could be involved somehow.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If this has something to do with creating synthetic life... Would Albedo go that far for one of his experiments? No, that can't be!)

response.speaker: Investigate the Paper
response.text: Amid the notes is a map with a few markings on it. Two of the marked locations correspond to the crime scenes, and the third appears to be in Dragonspine.

response.speaker: Investigate the Paper
response.text: It's a hard pill to swallow, but if the results of the joint investigation are correct, there could be a body hidden in that last location... Or, at the very least, what remains of one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, what does this mean? Do you think something might also be buried at the last location?

dialogues.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
dialogues.text: Dodo! Dodo! Dodoco!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Venti's calling! Let's answer!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: How's the investigation going? Find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found stuff alright... Stuff that only makes Albedo look even more suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I see... So, Albedo's researching something that doesn't help his case, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share what you learned with Venti...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Not promising... We should be grateful Albedo's true identity remains hidden. If it gets out that he's one of Rhinedottir's creations... there'd be no separating him from her past.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As we both know, Rhinedottir's approach to alchemy and ethics was pure madness, and the evidence you just found... Let's just say it could convince even those closest to him of his guilt. Perhaps, even you...

choices.text: I don't think the handwriting was faked...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Then, it comes down to trust... Do you trust Albedo?

choices.text: I don't know, but I want to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! He's our friend! We should keep the faith!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And, if he really is the culprit, he must have had a reason, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe he's just not allowed to talk about it... Yeah, that must be it!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Either way, a fair investigation means coming to a conclusion presented by the facts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Does that mean even Venti no longer believes in him?)

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Remaining objective has its own value. Remember — none of this is your fault. Just report back with an honest assessment of the facts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's go find Jean and tell her what we learned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that's... Miles! What's he doing here?

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Oh, ahem, sorry! I heard voices and wasn't sure if I should check who was inside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay — we're here on Jean's orders.

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Ah, I see. I'll leave you to it, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, you didn't hear what we were saying, did you?

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Oh, uh... Not really. Nothing that made sense, anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, do us a favor, and just forget anything you might've heard, okay?

response.speaker: Miles
response.text: Oh, sure. You got it.

choices.text: And the notes also sounded like him.

talks.objective: Go to the location marked out on the map

dialogues.speaker: Carefully examine the ground
dialogues.text: Although everything is covered in snow, as a seasoned adventurer, you notice a spot on the ground that looks quite different from its surroundings.

dialogues.speaker: Carefully examine the ground
dialogues.text: You remove the snow and find a sizeable hole underneath, large enough to fit a human body.

dialogues.speaker: Carefully examine the ground
dialogues.text: But, the hole is completely empty, and the surrounding markings make it look like something was dug up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Did an animal do this? Or some monster?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird... There's a hole but no body...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The prosecution's argument is that Albedo used alchemy to destroy the bodies, but this location is different from the other two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why not fill the hole or smooth out the ground like the other places?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If one person did all this... why not remove the traces like the others? And if Albedo isn't the one responsible, why was this location marked in his notes?)

talks.objective: Return to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: You're back. Did you find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but... none of it helps Albedo's case.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Jean about your findings from Albedo's office...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: A complicated result, but your efforts are appreciated.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did Albedo submit an appeal?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Yes, he asked for a retrial.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: There are still questions surrounding the identities of the victims and the disappearance of the bodies...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The minimal remains that were uncovered have been sent for forensic analysis, which should provide some answers. It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: If the victims turn out to be Mondstadt citizens, the situation becomes all the more serious. The second trial would likely have to be opened to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: And I doubt public sentiment will be in Albedo's favor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, not when the charges are so serious... *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The second trial is set to take place in two days. I hope you consider attending this one as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course, we'll be there. In the meantime, we should all just... stay positive.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Well said. When the time comes, I'll carry out my duty to the best of my ability.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Miles...

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I'll find a way and work things out.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: Should I turn my attention to Captain Kaeya? *sigh*... But, it's not like Master Diluc did anything wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm guessing Albedo has a plan. So, I should help him out.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But, what does he want me to do? Announce a break in the case? No... I should play it safe.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Since I made an honest assessment of the facts, I should be honest about my doubts, too. It's only fair...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Besides, I think I understand what Albedo was trying to tell me just now.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to address the court, if I may... I was the one who investigated the office, and I believe the results raise a few questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Regarding the two cases addressed in the previous trial, it was established that, after disposing of the bodies, the defendant used alchemy to restore the ground to its original state.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, that wasn't the case at the third location. The hole was still there, with dirt scattered around the perimeter — it looked more like something had been dug up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If this was all done by one person... Why wasn't the third scene given the same treatment as the others? Why weren't the traces removed?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In addition, the markings around the third location weren't fresh, which suggests that the Dragonspine incident happened at a different time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For those reasons, I believe there's still reasonable doubt in this case, and I hope the verdict reflects that. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Astute as ever, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Questions there may be, but allow me to point out... There is no evidence to suggest that anyone besides the defendant knew about the third location, and the map was found in his notes.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: That fact alone makes him the most plausible suspect. Unless Mr. Albedo suddenly plans to deny that the map belongs to him?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Allow me to respond to {NICKNAME}'s point.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If all I cared about was proving my innocence, I would indeed do as you described, Miss Hertha, and deny any connection to that map.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But, that is not what I intend to do... The map does belong to me, and I did hide things at those three locations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: There were indeed bodies at each location, and I did kill and bury someone on Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Hah, so you admit it! Let the record reflect that the defendant has confessed to his crimes!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You're mistaken, Miss Hertha. The story doesn't end there.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Some time ago, I encountered an uninvited guest on Dragonspine, someone who wanted to take advantage of the deserted nature of the region to eliminate me in secret.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: His desire to kill me led to an altercation where I killed him instead... and buried the body on the mountain — the third location marked on the map.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: #Actually, {NICKNAME}, Amber, Bennett, and I were with Albedo that day.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: The Adventurers' Guild was holding an event on Dragonspine. After it ended, we all left the area.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: If the person Albedo is referring to is different from the one we encountered on the mountain, then... the altercation must have occurred after we left.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: This only proves that the defendant is guilty on all counts! Those innocent people... Their blood is on your hands!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No, you're wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: You deny it? After admitting to murder for the whole court to hear? You've clearly lost your mind!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If you would let me finish, Miss Hertha... I could get to the important part.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The man who attacked me on Dragonspine was my height, with blond hair and blue eyes, dressed in clothes nearly identical to mine...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: So, someone who happens to look exactly like you?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Exactly like him...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, I was right! It does come back to what happened back then!)

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: It's one thing to look similar. But, for the clothes to be the same...?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: What's going on...? I don't wanna be here anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Regardless, the important thing is that you admit to killing someone on Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, I killed someone that day... someone who looked nearly identical to me.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But, I never said that someone was a "person."

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I see. Then, it appears I need to withdraw my testimony.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Note
dialogues.text: Everyone! I brought her!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Wait, you—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... The person who just came in... Isn't that Hertha?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Wh—What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: Who are you? Wh—Why do you wear my face?
Hello to you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As you can see, this is Hertha, the Logistics Captain of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: I see what's going on here... It's all been leading up to this, hasn't it? Your confession... It was all an elaborate stunt to set me up!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: You want to undermine my credibility? Fine! It doesn't eliminate the mountain of evidence stacked against you! All I want is justice for the people of Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Order in the court!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I've been stationed on Dragonspine all these years because that is where the subject of my research lies — the dragon, Durin.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Several hundred years ago, the Dragon of the East, Dvalin, defeated Durin in battle and, with help from Barbatos, sealed his remains on Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Durin was created through alchemy — one of the finest specimens of artificial life. As such, death was not a true end for him. His heart still beats and grows more revitalized by the day.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: My imposter on Dragonspine was a failed specimen abandoned in Durin's stomach, an unsuccessful iteration of the Homunculus Project.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Homunculus!?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: Are you trying to insinuate that I'm some kind of... homunculus? Because it looks to me like the artificial one is standing right there, some kind of imposter you dragged in from Dragonspine!
Haha, so this is what I look like when I fly off the handle...
Y'know, they say imitation is the best form of flattery, but your impersonation has overstayed its welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: Master Jean, what are you waiting for? We've known each other for so long. You recognize the real me, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The two of you look identical, but judging based on demeanor...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The new arrival actually seems more like the Hertha I know.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: That means nothing! By that logic, I could just as easily accuse the Albedo in this room of being an imposter!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: How do we know he isn't the fake one? A cold-blooded killer who replaced the real Albedo long ago!
Then, how about something only the real Hertha would know? The longest scar on my body... The Knights who fought alongside me that day should remember where it is.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I remember. Let's hear your answer.
I'd like to hear Miles answer first.

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, um...
You don't know? Or, you don't remember? I heard you've been acting strange these days — disoriented, confused...
You were closer to me than anyone during that battle, and yet you don't remember a thing... Strange indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: No! I... Argh! My head... It hurts...
The scar is right here.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Why the nerves? I can't imagine this comes as a surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Unless your informant in the Knights of Favonius failed to mention the scar on Hertha's left arm...
Albedo has done a lot of research into beings like you. If you deny it, then show us your arm.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No need to panic. You can just add it now. You excel at changing your appearance, don't you? Or, I should say, all spawn of Durin's life force have that ability.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A powerful life force, an appearance you can change at will... Yet, here you stand, formless one, paralyzed to act... Because you're worried using that power could affect your accomplices...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Accomplices... Then, Miles must be one of them!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: There are others, too. Most of the beings under the influence of Durin's life force have gathered here. And, yet, their presence is what impedes her from taking action.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Once you attempt to transform, all who surround you will be affected by your power. You can't control it, because in this network of living beings, you serve as the core.
Show us your arm!

dialogues.speaker: Hertha...?
dialogues.text: ...Ugh... Have it your way!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, they're shielding the imposter!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: She's trying to get away. Stop her! Don't let anyone stand in your way!

dialogues.speaker: Note
dialogues.text: There are others trying to get in! Must be more people under her control!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Time to get moving, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! She just leaped across the room!

dialogues.speaker: Note
dialogues.text: After her!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's time.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: All units move out! 3rd Company, keep on the imposter's tail!

dialogues.speaker: Note
dialogues.text: Roger that! We'll follow the plan!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We finally have a chance to talk. But, before I explain the events of the past few days, I'd like to make a few things clear.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: First, I never killed any of my fellow citizens, and I never used human remains as part of an alchemical experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Second, the events of the past few days were all part of a plan. Most of the members of our order were in on it. As for the witnesses, Master Diluc picked up on the situation long before today's proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wow, that's quite an... involved plan.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Indeed. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Welcome to Mondstadt, traveler. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Known as both "The Crown of the North" and "The City of Pastoral Song," there are no words that can truly describe the beauty of this city.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: A new bard arrived in the city not long ago. You should seek him out if you want to feel the true essence of Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: But the songs he plays are... a bit archaic?

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: ...Those songs date back thousands of years. No clue as to how he knows them...

choices.text: Are there any legends about Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: You've come to the right person.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: It's said in Mondstadt, a righteous hero often appears at night.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: But no one knows his true identity...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: I should stop there, or else I'll keep talking about him. If the Acting Grand Master catches me chatting on duty again...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Sorry, guess I'll talk to you next time.

choices.text: Are there any anecdotes about Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Anecdotes...? Not sure if this counts as one.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: When I'm on my shift here, I'll sometimes notice the weather change very suddenly.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Um... Rather than a natural phenomenon, it feels more like someone is manipulating the weather. But who has that much power to do that?

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Even the higher-ranking knights in the Knights of Favonius don't seem to have the ability to do that. How strange.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Goodbye, traveler. Hope you have a good time in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Wagner
dialogues.text: So many people seem out of it lately.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Really? It's been business as usual for me...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ah, you two. Let me know if you're ready, and we'll head out.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Alright, follow me.

choices.text: I have something to take care of first.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Of course. Let me know when you're done.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we now convene for the second trial against Mr. Albedo. I, Jean Gunnhildr, will once again oversee the proceedings.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Representatives on both sides remain unchanged, and Mr. Dahlia will continue to serve as assessor.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Miss Hertha represents the prosecution, and Mr. Kaeya speaks on behalf of the defense.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The defendant in this case is Mr. Albedo, Captain of the Investigation Team. With that, I now bring this trial to order.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Miss Hertha, have the investigators made any new discoveries?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Yes. We sent the teeth and the femur bone found at the scene to the Church's medical office and were able to conclude that these are, in fact, human remains.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: In addition, the investigators were able to identify several Mondstadt citizens who appear to have been missing for quite some time.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Forensic analysis of the remains allowed us to pinpoint the age and gender of the deceased. Interestingly, one of the missing individuals matches that profile to a tee.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: The medical office couldn't spare the personnel, so Miss Rosaria is here to present the results to the court.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Hanselmann, male, forty-six years old. Marital status — single. Occupation — hunter. Consistent with the conclusion in the last trial, his disappearance went unreported, likely due to his lack of relatives.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: In addition, medical records show that he sustained a mechanism-related injury to his leg three years ago. The damage on the femur bone Mr. Diluc found is consistent with such an injury.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Therefore, we can conclude that one of the victims in this case is Hanselmann. A specialized technique was likely used to accelerate the rate of decomposition.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Is it reasonable to assume this technique to be alchemical in nature?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Alchemical or magical... Both are possible.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Thank you for your testimony.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The identity of one of the victims is now confirmed. But, what about the defendant's motive?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Considering what he wrote in the letter, we can deduce that the defendant needed subjects for an alchemy experiment — who better than individuals whose disappearance would go unnoticed?

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: In other words, he sacrificed the good people of Mondstadt for his own gain... A truly vile act.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: In addition, another witness has agreed to testify. Miss Donna, if you would...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: ...Not good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Donna from the flower shop?

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I... I'm sorry it took me so long to come forward, but the night Master Diluc saw Mr. Albedo, I... was there too.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I was camping with a friend, and we decided to stop near Dragonspine. I couldn't really get comfortable that night, so around dawn, I decided to go for a walk, and that's when I saw Master Diluc.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I... thought it might be nice to, y'know, chat, so I headed in his direction, and then I saw it... Someone at the bottom of the cliff was getting rid of a body.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I was terrified the person might see me. Even after I fled, I couldn't shake that fear, and I... started to wish I never had a crush on Master Diluc in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: If I hadn't wanted to talk to him, I would never have been in that situation...

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I didn't want to come forward because I was scared. But, Miss Hertha convinced me it was the right thing to do. I... I'm sorry it took so long.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Just stepping forward was brave enough, Miss Donna.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The court thanks you for your courage and commitment to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: Ah... yes! Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The two witnesses corroborate the same sequence of events. That just leaves the question of how the defendant disposed of the bodies.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: I believe the answer lies in the alchemical technique mentioned in the letter. The defendant is the most accomplished alchemist in Mondstadt — he has the skill, no question.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: A special investigator also uncovered some relevant evidence on that subject. I will now present it to the court.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, does she mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The evidence we found in Albedo's office...)

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The following are pieces of evidence uncovered in Mr. Albedo's office. The most important of which... is this map.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jean presents the map you found in the hidden compartment. The marked locations stand out on the page, the weight of their secrets laid bare for all to see...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This map was found with the defendant's notes. The markings correspond with the description in the letter and the locations of the crime scenes.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Does this map belong to you?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Were you the one who marked these locations?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: You do realize that's basically an admission of guilt, don't you? The evidence against you is nearly insurmountable.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since you uncovered that compartment, I might as well expound on the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: We have witnesses and physical evidence, what could you possibly say in your defense?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What I always have. I never killed a single person.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Ugh, you have some nerve, saying that when the evidence is stacked against you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Miss Hertha, you've presented a meticulous and convincing case, I'll give you that. But, I will not admit to something I didn't do.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: So, what? You're just going to bombard the court with excuses?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's a rather dismissive way to refer to an innocent man speaking in his own defense. Besides, I'm not making excuses — I'm exercising patience.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: That won't make the charges against you disappear, Mr. Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Perhaps not, but patience comes with its own reward. It's easy for things to remain buried in snow... until someone comes along and brushes it away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Albedo seems serious, but unfazed. Does that mean he really didn't do anything untoward?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He mentioned, "brushing off the snow"... Is that supposed to be a hint?)

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you were the one who uncovered this map, right? Then, I'm assuming you've visited the third location as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Can you tell us what you found?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You nod your head and give an honest account of the scene you found on Dragonspine.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Whatever was kept in the hole was gone, and the surrounding area bore the markings of an unknown creature. With everything covered in snow, no one knew there was something to discover in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Then, there must also have been a body!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Albedo seems serious, but unfazed. Does that mean he really didn't do anything untoward?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He mentioned, "brushing off the snow"... Is that supposed to be a hint?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If it was a hint, then it must have something to do with Dragonspine. Which reminds me, one of the locations marked on the map we found was in Dragonspine, wasn't it...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I need to think about this. What clues am I missing...)

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I suppose we're old pals, too, at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Indeed. Your companionship is like a breeze that lingers in the air, warm and familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: In all this time, I've never witnessed Lord Barbatos approach anything in a serious manner. Perhaps, this time, I'm in for something special...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Barbatos, serious? Haha, you give him too much credit.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Hardly. It's not blind faith, you know. I've always had unwavering belief in the Anemo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Is that so? I wonder what Barbatos thinks about that... You should pray to him and find out.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Good idea! I'll tell him I still haven't deciphered his drunken musings from our three trips to the tavern last month. His wisdom is sure to reveal itself in time...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, um... You know what? Forget about Barbatos, Dahlia. Treat me to a drink instead! You wouldn't refuse me, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: A dear friend like you? Never.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thank you for agreeing to investigate. We're counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Wyratt
dialogues.text: Since you have Master Jean's permission, you're free to investigate the office any time!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to the Knights of Favonius, doubts swirling in your mind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know what? The Windblume Festival should be coming up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't been to Mondstadt in a while. C'mon, let's go check up on all our old friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That map we found in the hidden compartment seems important. We should check out the marked location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should be getting close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Look, over there! Something seems off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should meet up with Jean. It's about time for the second trial.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The first marked location is near Mondstadt. Beatrice saw Albedo use alchemy to dig a hole and bury a body there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A single men's shoe and a torn piece of fabric were found in the bushes nearby. Taken together, this evidence seems to suggest that Albedo killed someone and concealed the body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The second marked location is between Dragonspine and Dawn Winery, where Diluc saw Albedo bury the body of an adult male.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Diluc described nearly the same events as Beatrice. There's no reason for them to collude against Albedo, so their testimony should be trustworthy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Diluc found teeth and a femur bone at the scene, and Donna confirmed his version of events because she was also there that night.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The two should have no reason to set Albedo up. Despite her crush, Donna wouldn't lie about something like that just to get Diluc's attention.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not to mention, Donna has been acting strange since before the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The third marked location is in Dragonspine. We only knew about it because we found the map in the hidden compartment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: During our investigation, Paimon and I discovered a hole beneath the snow, big enough to hide a human body. There were also claw marks around the outside.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, there was no body or any remains whatsoever.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: According to the forensic results, the teeth and femur bone belong to a Mondstadt citizen, and the witness accounts suggest that Albedo was the last person to come into contact with his body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did Albedo really use alchemy to reduce the body to a few bones? And does that mean he's the killer?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Albedo marked these three locations on the map found in the hidden compartment. There are some similarities and differences between them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Based on what we know, all three locations were likely used to hide bodies. The holes dug in each area certainly seem big enough.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, unlike the first two locations, there were claw marks around the hole in the third location, and no witnesses saw anything happen there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dragonspine is home to all manner of monsters and wild animals. Could some kind of creature have dug up the body? But, why wasn't that the case in the other locations?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The marks didn't look fresh, which means the hole at the third location has been there longer than the other two.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, if the hole at the third location wasn't made around the same time... Does that mean it's connected to a separate incident?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Most people know Albedo as an alchemist and the Captain of the Investigation Team.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, in truth, he's the Kreideprinz, a synthetic human created by one of the Five Sinners — "Gold" Rhinedottir.

dialogues.speaker: Player
